classification.difficultyReason: The student reads the 3-pets stack in each of two dot plots and adds them to get 4. They then form the fraction of that subtotal that belongs to Class 8A (3 of 4) and convert it to 75%. Combining two plots and choosing the correct denominator (the 3-pet students, not the whole class) goes beyond the single-plot reading in p23-q5. It is less demanding than p24-q7, which also involves building the table and plot and several derived percentages.

content.prompt: Students in Class 8A and Class 8B were asked how many pets they have.

answer.worked:
At 3 pets, there are $3$ students in Class 8A and $1$ in Class 8B.
$$3+1=4\text{ students}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What percentage of the students with 3 pets were in Class 8A?

answer.worked:
Of the $4$ students with 3 pets, $3$ were in Class 8A.
$$\frac{3}{4}\times100\%=75\%$$
